msg: Hello, I'm a solo traveler from Germany, staying in Cartagena for a week. I've never dived but I'm curious. Is there a way to just try it for a day?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Absolutely! The *Dive Mini Course* is a great one-day introduction for first-time divers. It includes theory and pool practice with an instructor, plus one reef dive in the ocean. No prior experience or certification is needed, and you’ll return to Cartagena the same day.

The trip meets at *Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m.* and includes boat transport and lunch.

You can choose your date and book here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

For a first time I'd recommend the *mini-course*: theory, practice in calm water and a sea dive with an instructor, no experience needed. If you want to get certified, there's the *PADI Open Water course*. Shall we go for the mini-course? 🤿

msg: Sounds good. Actually, I have a whole week, so if I enjoy it I'd like to get certified. How does that work, and would the mini course count towards it?
reply:
The mini-course is a one-day introduction and *doesn’t count toward certification*. If you enjoy it and want to get certified, the full *PADI Open Water course* is the course to take. It takes 2 days, requires staying overnight on the islands, and certifies you to dive with a certified buddy down to 18 m. The mini-course and Open Water course are separate, so you’d need to complete the full course to earn your certification.

If you'd like, I can help you book it: *Dive mini-course*. Shall we? 🌊

msg: In that case I'd rather skip the mini course and go straight to the Open Water course, since I have the time. What does it cost, and how do I book it? I'd leave from Cartagena.
reply:
Great choice! The PADI Open Water course is a 2-day certification course for beginners. It includes online theory, pool training, four certification dives with a PADI instructor, equipment for the practical sessions, boat transport from Cartagena, lunch on day one, and your PADI certification card.

You’ll need to stay at least one night on the Rosario Islands; accommodation isn’t included. The course price is shown below, and you can book through the link on the course card. Complete the PADI eLearning theory before the practical sessions.

🤿 *PADI Basic Course (Open Water)*
💰 *693 USD* per person (online rate)
📚 PADI course: dates, sessions and details are arranged with you.

👉 *For more information and to book, click here:*
https://book.divingplanet.org/book/basic-course/4?language=en

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

Is there anything else I can help you with? I can *add another activity*, answer questions, or adjust your booking. 🤿

msg: Perfect. Where do you suggest I stay on the island, and is there any chance to speak with someone from your team before I pay, to pick the dates and sort the eLearning?
reply:
For your Open Water course, you’ll need to stay at least one night on the Rosario Islands; accommodation isn’t included and is booked directly with the hotel. Our base hotels are *San Pedro de Majagua* and *Cocoliso* on Isla Grande, where pick-up is confirmed. Other nearby hotels with maritime access are *Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras, and Pao Pao*.

A team advisor can help with your request to discuss dates and eLearning before you pay.

I'll connect you with an advisor from the Diving Planet team.
They will contact you shortly. Thanks! :)
Noted 🙌 I've already passed your case to an advisor from the team: they can see this whole conversation and will write to you here shortly.
